pride_data.title: Proteomics analysis of lipid droplets proteins in ccRCC cells
pride_data.projectDescription: Deposition of lipid droplets (LDs) is a hallmark of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC).LD functions are regulated by a complement of integral and peripheral proteins that associate with the bounding LD phospholipid monolayer. By employing proximity labeling with TurboID fusion constructs which targeting to LD, we mapped LD proteome in live ccRCC cell lines. These data provide an important resource for future LD studies in ccRCC and other tumors.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Biotinylated LD proteins were enriched from cell lysate by using streptavidin-coated magnetic beads. To prepare samples for mass spectrometry analysis, proteins bound to streptavidin beads were washed and conducting on-bead digestion. The eluate was reduced with 4 mM DTT for 30 min at 25 °C with shaking. The samples were alkylated with 10 mM iodoacetamide for 45 min in the dark at 25 °C with shaking. An additional 0.5 μg of trypsin was added to the sample and the digestion was completed overnight at 25 °C with shaking. After overnight digestion, samples were acidified (to pH < 3) by adding FA such that the sample contained ~1% FA. Samples were desalted on C18 StageTips and evaporated to dryness in a vacuum concentrator, then resuspended in 0.1% FA. peptides were analyzed using a Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer coupled with the Easy-nLC 1000 system (Thermo Fisher Scientific). For each injection, 1 μg of peptides were loaded onto a 2-cm self-packed trap column (150 μm inner diameter, ReproSil-Pur C18-AQ, 3 μm; Dr Maisch) and separated on a 150 μm × 30 cm self-packed C18 analytical column (ReproSil-Pur C18-AQ,1.9 μm; Dr Maisch) using a gradient from 8% to 95% B with 120 min total run. Mobile phase A was 100% water with 0.1% FA, and mobile phase B was 80% acetonitrile. The instrument was operated in data independent acquisition (DIA) mode. The full scan was acquired from m/z 350 to 1,000 with a resolution of 60,000, AGC target of 1×106, followed by 38 MS2 scans of 200–2,000 m/z with 1.6 m/z isolation windows and 30,000 resolution.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: For protein identification and quantification of proteomic data from tissue samples, the tandem mass spectra were searched against the reviewed human UniProt database (version: 20180820, 20,325 sequences) using MaxQuant (version: 1.6.3.4). Trypsin was selected as the proteolytic enzyme, and two missed cleavages sites were allowed. Cysteine carbamidomethylation was set as a fixed modification. The oxidation of M and acetylation of the protein N-terminal were set as variable modifications. Peptides with the minimum of seven amino acid length were considered and the required FDR was set to 1% at the peptide and protein level. Match between run was applied with default parameters. The first search mass tolerance was 20 ppm, and the main search peptide tolerance was 4.5 ppm. Quantification in MaxQuant was performed using the Label-Free Quantification algorithm.
